notes:
Round 4 of the post-acceptance BIO-OPS-002 remediation. Zainab's audit-shape review confirmed round 3's envelope conversion, new-tenant source, canonical correlation handling, and DI registration were all sound - she found exactly one remaining gap: previous_tenant_id/previous_role_id were already constrained to closed allowlists (the 'alpha'/'beta' check and the ActorIdByRole.ContainsKey check) before being written to AuditEvent.Detail, but previous_actor_id was copied straight from the request body with no validation at all. Any holder of a genuinely valid synthetic demo session could therefore persist arbitrary caller-controlled text (personal data, a secret, an oversized string) into Detail at classification 'internal' - exactly what Kemi's own canonical-id/non-secret allowlist ruling was meant to prevent across the board, not just for two of the three previous_* fields.

Fix: previous_actor_id must now equal ActorIdByRole[previous_role_id] (when previous_role_id is present - the existing all-or-nothing previousFields check already guarantees it's present exactly when the others are) or the request is rejected with 400 previous_actor_id_role_mismatch. Critically, the value actually WRITTEN to Detail is the derived lookup result, not the caller's own string that happened to pass validation - this means even a value that is byte-for-byte identical to what the caller sent can never be traced back to 'the caller's string was trusted,' only to 'this endpoint's own lookup computed it,' which is the actual property Zainab's finding asked for ('derive it, don't trust the caller's value'), not merely 'reject anything that doesn't match.'

Also added, per Zainab's own explicit request, sink-level assertions that resolve the real InMemoryAuditSink singleton directly from the test host (the same GetRequiredService<InMemoryAuditSink>() pattern DeviceRegistryTests.cs already uses for its own IAuditSink-backed sink) and inspect the actually-STORED AuditEvent, not just the HTTP response: exact Detail key set (previous_tenant_id/previous_role_id/previous_actor_id/new_role_id, nothing more, nothing less), Device == null, Classification == 'internal', Outcome == Allowed, and both halves of the correlation-id behavior (a well-formed evt_ header is preserved verbatim; a malformed one is discarded and replaced with a fresh canonical evt_, confirmed via CanonicalId.IsWellFormed on the actually-recorded value, not just 'not equal to the garbage I sent'). The original 9 tests from rounds 1-3 only ever asserted the HTTP response shape (event_id/new_tenant_id/new_role_id/new_actor_id) - this was a genuine coverage gap Zainab correctly identified, not just a nice-to-have.

Verification: dotnet build clean (0 warnings/errors). 13/13 in DemoSessionContextAuditEndpointsTests.cs (was 9, +4: two mismatch-rejection tests - one using a different role's real actor id, one using arbitrary free text including an HTML/script-injection-shaped string to prove this isn't merely a shape check that a crafted payload could slip past - and two sink-level shape/correlation tests). Full Biolog.IntegrationTests 292/292 (was 288, +4, zero regression from this diff). One flaky, non-deterministic failure observed twice in ObservabilityTests.cs's own AC01 test during the full-suite run (two different failure modes across two runs: a StringBuilder.ToString ArgumentOutOfRangeException once, a null-vs-string assertion mismatch once) - root-caused by reading that test's own source: it swaps the process-wide Console.Out to capture log lines, which races against whatever OTHER test classes xUnit runs concurrently writing to the same global Console.Out at the same time. Confirmed as pre-existing and unrelated to this diff, not assumed: ran that test in isolation (passed cleanly, 9/9), then re-ran the FULL suite twice more (292/292 clean both times) - the flake is intermittent and keyed to concurrent test-class scheduling, not to anything in this change (which touches no logging/Console configuration at all). Did not attempt to fix ObservabilityTests.cs itself - out of scope, pre-existing, not asked for. Biolog.UnitTests 211/211 unchanged. module-reference/contract-freeze/secret-scan all PASS.

Process note: learned from round 3's own mistake - ran `git status --short` immediately after both the code `git add`+commit and before writing this evidence file, confirming no paths were silently dropped this time.

Orchestration: still DONE status, late-commit/builder-complete both refuse as in rounds 1-3 - committed directly on feature/BIO-TEN-002, tracked via this fourth per-round evidence file.
